item.title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01971-z

Climate action reshapes who gains and loses from energy and environmental resources, raising new geopolitical questions. A study now quantifies four climate-related asset types across 169 countries and reveals uneven asset redistribution, with major powers often less affected.
item.dc:title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation

item.title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01939-z

Deforestation-reducing development pathways may cut emissions, but it is unclear how workers can adapt given skill and geographic mobility constraints. Modelling job transitions in Brazil reveals that greener pathways benefit workers in high-skill occupations but increase low-skill unemployment, mitigated by mobility policies.
item.dc:title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil

item.title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01951-3

Choosing a feasible economic growth trajectory to mitigate climate change cannot hinge on only gross domestic product trends. This Perspective presents a framework to understand where each possible growth path places its heaviest burdens and shows that such understanding is critical to inform policy decisions.
item.dc:title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
item.dc:creator: Ingo Pies
Felix Carl Schultz
